structured_output.summary: One PR: add a process-wide detached-stream registry keyed by upstream, stream_detached and stream_logs options, hijack-safe recorder/encode/intercept, stream metrics, docs, and unit plus integration tests. Docs live in Go doc comments (generated docs), no separate doc files.

intents.rationale: No detached mode exists; connections are tracked per Handler and closed in Cleanup. Need a process-wide registry keyed by upstream so detached streams outlive the handler and are closed only when their upstream disappears.
Default behaviour must be preserved while refactoring; existing cleanupConnections/StreamCloseDelay logic stays for non-detached streams and needs a regression test.

No stream_logs config exists. Add StreamLogs (skip_handshake, level, logger_name) to Handler and Caddyfile; skip_handshake sets the existing log_skip var; close logs go to the access logger when logger_name is access.

responseRecorder.Hijack wraps the conn in hijackedConn counting bytes via the recorder, and encode/intercept may write after hijack. Proxy must use the raw conn, 101 must be final, wrappers must no-op after hijack.
Extended CONNECT path (h2ReadWriteCloser) must keep working and join the new stream lifecycle; HTTP/1.1 detached must work. Needs tests.
Only upstreams_healthy exists; add active streams gauge, closed counter by result, duration histogram, and bytes counters per direction, recorded once per stream.
Document new options in the Caddyfile syntax comment and JSON field comments.
Add real-server integration tests; stream_test.go covers only h2 to h2c streaming.
Add unit tests for registry, parsing, metrics, recorder, encode and intercept changes.

criteria.text: With stream_detached, an established Upgrade stream keeps passing data after a config reload; when the reload removes its upstream that stream is closed while streams to retained upstreams stay open.
Caddyfile and JSON stream_detached both set Handler.StreamDetached and survive Caddyfile-to-JSON adaptation.
Without stream_detached an upgraded stream is closed on reload; with stream_close_delay it stays open until the delay elapses, then closes.

stream_logs with skip_handshake, level and logger_name parse from Caddyfile and JSON; defaults are handshake logged and level DEBUG; skip_handshake suppresses the access log entry for the upgrade request.
With logger_name access, a stream close log entry appears in the access log at the configured level, including duration and byte counts.
WebSocket upgrades through encode and through intercept with handle_response work end to end; the client receives exactly one 101 and no writes happen to the response after hijack.
The proxy copies stream bytes on the raw hijacked connection, so the recorder size is not inflated by stream bytes.
HTTP/2 extended CONNECT WebSocket through reverse_proxy transfers data, and an HTTP/1.1 upgrade works in detached mode.
Active-streams, closed-by-result, duration and bytes-to/from-backend metrics are updated, and each stream is counted exactly once even when both directions end, time out or are closed by cleanup.
Doc comments on the Handler JSON fields and the Caddyfile syntax block describe stream_detached, stream_logs, skip_handshake and the log level.
Integration tests with a real server and clients cover reload survive/close in both modes, h2 extended CONNECT, upgrades via encode and intercept, and detached streams with access logging.
Unit tests cover the registry, config parsing, metrics, recorder hijack behaviour, and encode and intercept post-hijack behaviour; existing suites stay green.

tasks.summary: Order: (1) hijack safety in caddyhttp recorder, encode and intercept; (2) new stream registry (detached.go) plus StreamDetached/StreamLogs fields, Provision/Cleanup and handleUpgradeResponse using raw conn; (3) metrics; (4) Caddyfile parsing and docs; (5) unit tests then integration tests. Default non-detached path keeps closeConnections/StreamCloseDelay unchanged.
